gaps.note: The product (D_{a_k}D_{a_{k-1}}^{-1})...(D_{a_1}D_{a_0}^{-1}) telescopes to D_{a_k}D_{a_0}^{-1}, not D_{a_k}D_{a_1}^{-1}: the innermost D_{a_1}^{-1} cancels against D_{a_1} of the next factor and D_{a_0}^{-1} remains. The page's right-hand side is wrong and inconsistent with the later 'D_sink D_source^{-1}' (source = first node alpha_0). The paper (lines 143-145) states the route applies D_{sink(rho(w))} D_{source(w)}^{-1}.

The page uses D_nu^{-1} (edge operator D_beta D_alpha^{-1}) but only says the frame is a linear operator. The hypothesis that each frame is invertible is missing; the paper (line 132) chooses an invertible linear operator.

gaps.term: scalar network is a signed role permutation
gaps.quote: Let $\rho$ be the permutation of roles that it applies
gaps.note: The page's network consists of linear steps (with scratch roles whose values are added and restored) and it is never said why its net scalar map is a signed permutation of roles. The paper (lines 818-819) uses this only as a hypothesis ('if the scalar network is a signed role permutation'); the page asserts it as a fact about every network without stating it as a hypothesis.

gaps.quote: By the telescoping, the route applies
gaps.note: The telescoped edge operators act on stored arrays, so D_source^{-1} appears only because the supplied input array is taken as the stored array at the source, i.e. the logical input is D_source^{-1} applied to it (paper lines 141-142 and 804-806). The page never states how the input array is interpreted, so the reader cannot see why the route applies the endpoint operator to the input array.

gaps.quote: its operator is $D_\nu$, however many gates it passes through
gaps.note: The page just said the route applies epsilon_w D_sink D_source^{-1}; with source frame I and sink frame D_nu the operator is epsilon_w D_nu, and equals D_nu only when the sign is +1. The example omits the sign, inconsistent with the earlier statement (paper line 821: epsilon_w D_sink D_source^{-1}).
